newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money rates rise on tight allocation.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money rates rise on tight allocation.

text.p: Dutch call money rates rose after a tight allocation on Friday, but dealers said the increase was temporary because of an expected new influx of payments into the market after the weekend.
Call money rates were bid between 2.68 and 2.75 percent from 2.56 percent on Thursday.
The Dutch central bank allocated 2.21 billion guilders to the money market this morning under a six-day pact at an unchanged rate of 2.50 percent.
"Participants had to sift through the money market for extra liquidity," said one dealer.
Dealers said most trades were in the shorter end, with few offers in long-dated guilder deposits.
"Trade focused on call and deposits up to three months," said another dealer, adding business was likely to fizzle out in the afternoon before the weekend.
Traders said they were cautious on the outcome of next week's U.S. Fed meeting with most participants expecting a 25 basis point hike in the discount rate.
"But a rise in U.S interest rates will not have any real effect on the Dutch money market," said one dealer, adding the direction of rates in Germany was more important.
Dealers were divided on whether Germany's current rates were at the bottom.
Three-month deposits were unchanged at 2.70 percent bid.
The guilder slipped a little against the mark to trade at 112.10 per 100 marks versus 112.08 on Thursday.
"We start worrying as soon as the exchange rate surpasses the 112.11 per 100 marks," said one dealer, adding the current drop of the guilder had no impact on the money market.
